note: Levels: Foundation 0, Core 4, Advanced 8. last_verified is null because source files record YYYY-MM, not a full day. Outcomes are the lesson summaries.

lessons.title: Five routing methods
outcomes: Standard, predictive, bullseye, preferred agent, and conditional group routing are the methods on a queue.

lessons.title: All skills, best available, or disregard
outcomes: The evaluation method is how standard and bullseye decide that an agent “has the skills.”

lessons.title: Conversation score and priority score
outcomes: One priority point on conversation score is worth 60,000 milliseconds of arrival time.

lessons.title: Bullseye rings widen the target
outcomes: Up to five rings. A delay from 2 seconds to 72 hours. Up to 50 skills removed on a ring.

lessons.title: Preferred agents are tried first
outcomes: A preferred agent is considered even without the required skills, and only if they are a member of the queue and On Queue.

lessons.title: Predictive routing is a KPI model with a timeout
outcomes: Predictive routing can run for everyone, in a comparison test, or at a fixed 80/20 split you cannot edit.

lessons.title: Conditional group routing borrows agents carefully
outcomes: A rule is a KPI plus agent availability. The other queue must be able to spare the people.

lessons.title: Utilization and Not Responding
outcomes: A fully utilized agent is skipped. An agent who ignores an alert becomes Not Responding.

lessons.title: Two Architect bot types, plus Copilot beside the agent
outcomes: A bot flow talks to the customer. Agent Copilot talks to the agent. They are different products on different pages.

lessons.title: Dialog Engine bot flows are voice and digital intents
outcomes: You build the bot in Architect, then the inbound flow calls it.

lessons.title: Digital bot flows are a different call
outcomes: Message experiences use Digital Bot Flows and Call Digital Bot Flow.

lessons.title: Every bot has a failure output to a queue
outcomes: No-match, timeout, and error are normal. The queue is the design.

lessons.title: Agent Copilot assists the person who stayed on the interaction
outcomes: Knowledge, transcripts, scripts, next best action, and notes. The benefit is described as surviving a blind transfer.

lessons.title: Tokens are a published allotment, and a FAQ ratio you re-read
outcomes: The overview publishes CX 4 token counts. The STA FAQ publishes how AI scoring spends them.

lessons.title: The AI exams are named on the catalog, one exam each
outcomes: Two AI certifications. No invented exam codes.

lessons.title: The Developer Center is the map. This lab is not a client.
outcomes: Read the public docs. Do not point a tutorial at a production org.

lessons.title: Pick the grant that matches who the call runs as
outcomes: Client credentials, authorization code with PKCE, and SAML2 Bearer are the grants to learn. Implicit is the one leaving.

lessons.title: Client credentials have no user, so users/me is the wrong call
outcomes: The token is the client. The guide shows that limit on purpose.

lessons.title: Implicit grant is a migration, not a new design
outcomes: The OAuth article dates the deprecation: after 25 May 2026.

lessons.title: Login host and API host are a pair you look up
outcomes: US East is the pair this lab will quote in full. Other rows stay on the regions article.

lessons.title: Role and division pairs are the real permission
outcomes: A token opens the door the role allows, in the division the pair names.

lessons.title: SCIM and other directory sync still start with an OAuth client
outcomes: The OAuth article points SCIM at a client. The client still has roles and a grant.

lessons.title: The flow types on the Architect home page
outcomes: Architect is a list of flow types. Picking the wrong tab is the first defect.

lessons.title: Tasks, menus, and a way out
outcomes: An inbound call flow plays audio, collects input, and must transfer, hand off, or disconnect.

lessons.title: In-queue flows are the hold experience
outcomes: The caller is already queued. The in-queue flow is what they hear or read while ACD looks for an agent.

lessons.title: Data actions and participant data
outcomes: A data action calls a system outside the flow. Participant data carries a value to the agent.

lessons.title: Common modules are how you stop copying tasks
outcomes: A common module is a flow type you call from other flows. The name is still unique inside that type.

lessons.title: Secure call flows keep digits away from the recording
outcomes: A secure flow is how a caller enters a card number without that audio being recorded or shown to the agent.

lessons.title: Call a bot from the inbound flow
outcomes: Dialog Engine bot flows and digital bot flows are Architect flow types. The inbound flow calls them. It does not become them.

lessons.title: Publish, division, and Flow Insights
outcomes: A saved flow is a draft. The runtime uses the published version. Insights tell you whether anyone hit it.

lessons.title: BYOC Cloud is your carrier, Genesys’ media
outcomes: You bring the carrier contract. Genesys terminates a SIP trunk on the AWS media tier. Audio is RTP on the internet.

lessons.title: Carrier trunks and PBX trunks
outcomes: BYOC Carrier and BYOC PBX are the two types. Carrier has subtypes. PBX has one.

lessons.title: The quick-start order
outcomes: Location, trunk, outbound route, number plan. The product on the subscription comes before all of that.

lessons.title: Dynamic Cloud Voice is the current platform
outcomes: New trunks start there. Moving an old trunk means allow lists, Amazon root CAs, TLS ciphers, and a toggle.

lessons.title: Number plans classify what people dial
outcomes: A site can hold 200 plans. DIDs do not need one for basic routing. Emergency, extension, and 988 already exist as defaults.

lessons.title: Watch the trunk, not only the flow
outcomes: When audio fails and Architect Insights still shows runs, the trunk is the next object.

lessons.title: Genesys Cloud Voice is the other door
outcomes: If Genesys is the carrier, you buy numbers in a region that offers voice, and emergency is part of that product story rather than your trunk.

lessons.title: AppFoundry is the marketplace, not a feature you assume is installed
outcomes: An app is present only after someone installs it into the org.

lessons.title: Genesys Cloud for Salesforce is a documented embed
outcomes: Screen pop, click-to-dial, logging, and the assist features that page names.

lessons.title: Salesforce data actions move to OAuth client credentials
outcomes: Consumer key, secret, and My Domain URL. The request body of the action stays.

lessons.title: Zendesk has its own about page, with a similar embed idea
outcomes: Do not copy the Salesforce field list onto Zendesk.

lessons.title: Dynamics, ServiceNow, and the rest stay on the marketplace
outcomes: No invented feature lists for CRMs this lab did not open.

lessons.title: A CRM failure is not an ACD failure
outcomes: Screen pop can die while the queue is healthy.

lessons.title: The conversation crosses a short list of systems
outcomes: Carrier, trunk or Edge, Architect, queue, agent, then the systems beside the agent.

lessons.title: WFM, QM, E911, analytics, CRM, and bots are sisters
outcomes: Each sister has a track and a page. None of them is a setting on the queue tab alone.

lessons.title: The Cisco bridge is a translation, with both citations showing
outcomes: UCCE, UCCX, CUCM, and Webex are named so a Cisco engineer can find the door.

lessons.title: Read the catalog by name, then the announcement
outcomes: GC-GCP and GC-GCD are catalog codes. Specialist rows are names. AI rows are two exams.

lessons.title: Interview answers cite a page, not a vibe
outcomes: The drill in this lab is a set of questions with a model answer and a link.

lessons.title: What this lab will not invent
outcomes: Prices, unconfirmed hosts, exam codes, lifecycle dates, and CRM feature lists stay off the page.

lessons.title: The telephony door this lab can cite is BYOC, not a word the page did not use
outcomes: CPaaS is the classroom name for a communications API you bring. The opened page is About BYOC Cloud.

lessons.title: Salesforce and Zendesk are the embeds this lab opened
outcomes: Salesforce Open CTI is in maintenance and has a later retirement date. Zendesk’s page does not say that.

lessons.title: A bot, a Virtual Agent, and Copilot are three assists
outcomes: Dialog Engine builds the bot. Virtual Agent adds Genesys AI. Copilot sits with the person.

lessons.title: Future hooks are dates on announcements, not a roadmap this lab invented
outcomes: Journey Outcomes, Salesforce Open CTI, and Customer Outcomes are three different sentences.

lessons.title: The premises Edge is the local media hop
outcomes: BYOC Premises puts an Edge on your network. Phones and trunks registered there do not need a public address the way BYOC Cloud does.

lessons.title: Local site routing stays home until it cannot
outcomes: Genesys uses Edges in the same site when it can. Another site is the exception.

lessons.title: Phone trunks, WebRTC, and inherit
outcomes: WebRTC and SIP phones are phone trunks on the Edge group. Inherit is the default you should verify.

lessons.title: When the local Edge is offline
outcomes: The documented failover is another site, if that site actually has the resource.

lessons.title: Choose Cloud, Premises, or both
outcomes: Use premises when the phones and the carrier are on your network. Use cloud when they are not. Use both only where each number has an owner.

lessons.title: A browser phone is still a network endpoint
outcomes: WebRTC removes the desk set. It does not remove media engineering.

lessons.title: Premises turn-up checklist
outcomes: Group, inherit, site, trunk, failover test, emergency owner.

lessons.title: Name the emergency owner before the DID
outcomes: Genesys is not responsible for emergency calls that ride a BYOC trunk. That sentence belongs in the design, not in the postmortem.

lessons.title: Emergency is a classification and a route
outcomes: The default Emergency plan matches 911 and 933 in the US and Canada, and 142 in Switzerland. It still needs a route.

lessons.title: The location is a physical place
outcomes: The quick start adds a location because services, including emergency, need a real site.

lessons.title: Voice coverage is a table, not a promise
outcomes: Country rows decide DID, toll-free, domestic, and international. FedRAMP and the sovereign region add harder edges.

lessons.title: Normalize toward E.164 on purpose
outcomes: Intra-country and inter-country plans normalize. Digit-length extensions and E.164 lists do not.

lessons.title: Test emergency like a change, not like a demo
outcomes: A live emergency test is a carrier and public-safety conversation. The call simulator is the part you can do alone.

lessons.title: A forecast is a WFM plan for interactions, not a routing method
outcomes: Workforce management is one WEM product. The forecast article names the metrics and the permissions.

lessons.title: Short-term weeks can schedule. Long-term weeks cannot
outcomes: Six weeks of intervals on one side. Up to two years of days and weeks on the other.

lessons.title: Four creation methods, and a 130-week outer limit
outcomes: Automatic best method, weighted history, imported source days, or a finished short-term file.

lessons.title: The editor shows history as read-only lines
outcomes: Short-term granularity is 15, 30, or 60 minutes. Long-term granularity is daily or weekly.

lessons.title: The schedule has to sit inside the short-term weeks
outcomes: Generation offers a forecast only when those weeks cover the schedule, and only one schedule is generated at a time.

lessons.title: Use the forecast, then go back to the floor
outcomes: Intraday compares the plan with what happened. Adherence is a different WFM page.

lessons.title: What Genesys Cloud CX is
outcomes: Genesys Cloud CX is a subscription contact-center platform with four nested packages, not a single feature switch.

lessons.title: Core regions and satellite media
outcomes: An organization is born in one core AWS region. Satellite regions carry media. They do not host the org.

lessons.title: SIP, RTP, and what the trunk is doing
outcomes: SIP sets the call up. RTP moves the audio. They are different protocols, and Genesys trunks speak both.

lessons.title: What ACD is before you name a queue
outcomes: ACD picks an agent for a waiting interaction. The queue is the waiting line. Skills, utilization, and On Queue decide who is eligible.

lessons.title: Digital conversations beside voice
outcomes: Voice is one media. Architect also has inbound message, email, and chat flows, and queues track those medias separately.

lessons.title: Divisions, before roles get complicated
outcomes: A division groups objects inside one organization. It is not a second org, and the Home division cannot be deleted.

lessons.title: How to read a Genesys page without inventing the rest
outcomes: This lab cites the Resource Center, the Developer Center, Genesys Education, and RFCs. The page wins when they differ.

lessons.title: Prerequisites before the first trunk
outcomes: BYOC Cloud needs a public carrier address, an open port plan, and a real location. The org subscription has to include the telephony product you intend to use.

lessons.title: Nothing imports your old routing by magic
outcomes: You rebuild flows, queues, and trunks. You do not flip a converter this lab has not found.

lessons.title: Engage and PureConnect become flows and queues
outcomes: Strategies, IRDs, and handlers are read as behavior, then redrawn.

lessons.title: IVR becomes Architect tasks, menus, and audio
outcomes: CVP, UCCX prompts, and Engage voice all become the same kind of flow.

lessons.title: UCCE skill groups and precision queues are not Genesys queues
outcomes: Membership, skills, and bullseye are three ideas you reassemble.

lessons.title: UCCX is a smaller center with the same rebuild rule
outcomes: Scripts, CSQs, and the Finesse desktop do not move as files.

lessons.title: CUCM stays. BYOC is the door, not a replacement cluster.
outcomes: A dial plan and a trunk are Genesys number plans and a BYOC trunk. CUCM is still yours.

lessons.title: Webex is a neighbor, not a page this lab pretends to summarize
outcomes: Use Cisco’s product pages. Do not cite a Webex help URL this lab did not confirm.

lessons.title: Cut over one number, then the queue, then the people
outcomes: A weekend big-bang is how untested emergency routes meet a full staff.

lessons.title: Place the organization in a core region
outcomes: You do not move an org between regions as a setting. You create it in a core region and live with that login host.

lessons.title: Roles are permission lists paired with divisions
outcomes: A role without a division grant does not open objects. An OAuth client inherits only a subset of its creator’s pairs.

lessons.title: Named licenses and the concurrent peak
outcomes: Concurrent billing charges the peak of simultaneous users, and it ignores peaks shorter than 30 minutes.

lessons.title: Pick CX 1, CX 2, CX 3, or CX 4 on purpose
outcomes: Match the package to the job. Do not buy CX 1 and then design a WFM project.

lessons.title: People, queues, and the 5,000 member line
outcomes: Users live in the org. Queue membership is not the same thing as a division, and it has a hard cap.

lessons.title: Fair use is a pool, not a mystery invoice
outcomes: Licenses include monthly allowances. Overage is priced on the policy page. Copying the numbers into a design doc freezes them wrong.

lessons.title: A first-week admin checklist
outcomes: Week one is region, divisions, roles, packages, one queue, and a published in-queue flow. Telephony can follow.

lessons.title: Predictive Engagement watches the site, not the queue math
outcomes: It predicts what a visitor is trying to do and offers a message, a chat, content, or a flow. Predictive routing is a different feature on the queue.

lessons.title: Messenger tracks web messaging. The old snippet tracks web chat.
outcomes: Genesys tells Genesys Cloud CX customers to use web messaging. Leaving both snippets on the page double-counts the visit.

lessons.title: A segment matches visitors who meet every condition you listed
outcomes: At least one condition. More conditions, fewer visitors. Conditions are not shared with the next segment.

lessons.title: An action map is qualified before it is offered
outcomes: Segment, visitor activity, and outcome probability are the trigger kinds. Priority breaks a tie. Web chat is the legacy action.

lessons.title: Journey Outcomes have a published end date
outcomes: Announced 18 May 2026. Planned effective date 29 June 2026. Outcome scoring is not part of the Customer Outcomes replacement.

lessons.title: An Architect flow can be the action, and it can also be the thing you must edit
outcomes: Advanced orchestration is an action type. Flows that still call getJourneyOutcome need a path that does not depend on it.

lessons.title: Prove the map with Live Now and the performance reports
outcomes: Visitor activity and action-map performance are the Predictive Engagement reports. Outcome columns age out with the deprecation.

lessons.title: Quality management evaluates the conversation
outcomes: QM records and scores interactions, and it can coach. It is not the schedule.

lessons.title: Forms have questions and weights
outcomes: The form is the rubric. Weights decide which questions move the score.

lessons.title: Recording policies choose calls and retention
outcomes: A policy decides which ACD calls are recorded and how long they are kept. A secure flow is a hole in a segment, not a substitute for the policy.

lessons.title: Coaching and disputes close the loop
outcomes: A score that the agent cannot see and cannot dispute is not a quality program.

lessons.title: AI scoring needs STA, QM, and tokens
outcomes: The FAQ is blunt: AI scoring requires Speech and Text Analytics, Quality Management, and AI Experience Tokens.

lessons.title: Retention, export, and the reason you recorded
outcomes: Export and AWS recording paths exist so a recording can leave the platform under a policy, not as a side copy.

lessons.title: Quality evaluates the interaction. Speech analytics reads it
outcomes: The quality article says speech and text analytics runs on 100 percent of interactions. That is a claim to re-open, not a sample size you invent.

lessons.title: A question is human, AI scored, or assisted by topics
outcomes: The form article names three automation choices. Evaluation focus is Full Interaction or Evaluated Agent.

lessons.title: AI scoring waits for history, and a low week hides the answer
outcomes: A rolling window of 25 submissions. Below 75 percent, the answer is hidden. The transcript needs 300 characters.

lessons.title: Phrases make a topic. Topics make a program
outcomes: A program is mapped to queues or flows, and it can turn sentiment and empathy on or off.

lessons.title: Programs have counts, and the organization switch wins
outcomes: One hundred programs. Five hundred topics per dialect. Twenty scoring rules. Sentiment off at the org turns it off everywhere.

lessons.title: Agent scoring picks which agent receives the evaluation
outcomes: Each, first, or last matched agent. The article also says the last participant is the evaluated agent.

lessons.title: Create the queue in a division
outcomes: The queue is a named waiting line in one division, with at most 5,000 members.

lessons.title: Skills and proficiency are on the agent
outcomes: The queue asks for skills. The agent profile holds them. Evaluation decides whether proficiency matters.

lessons.title: After call work and the system wrap-up codes
outcomes: ACW is optional, discretionary, or time-boxed. The platform has its own codes when agents do not finish.

lessons.title: Wrap-up codes live in divisions too
outcomes: The codes an agent sees are the codes their role can see, and Genesys wants them in the queue’s division.

lessons.title: Service level is a percentage and a target in seconds
outcomes: Each media has a service level percentage and a target duration. That pair is what conditional routing and WFM both mean by “the goal.”

lessons.title: Callbacks are interactions with their own rules
outcomes: A callback is queued work. It still needs a wrap-up code, and it counts as its own utilization slot.

lessons.title: Membership, On Queue, and the copy trap
outcomes: A copied queue can duplicate a bullseye you did not mean to clone.

lessons.title: ACD is the match, and skills are one way to make it
outcomes: Wikipedia describes an ACD as a distributor. Genesys Cloud puts that job on the queue’s routing method.

lessons.title: Three evaluation methods, and a seven-day lookback
outcomes: All skills matching, best available skills, and disregard skills do different jobs. Proficiency covers ACD skills and language skills together.

lessons.title: Bullseye widens the pool in two documented ways
outcomes: One way adds skill-expression groups. The other removes skills. The ring count is not the same sentence on every page.

lessons.title: A skill expression filter replaces the queue’s skill list
outcomes: It works for standard and predictive routing when evaluation is All skills matching. Other methods ignore it.

lessons.title: Direct routing still uses a queue
outcomes: The customer reaches a dedicated person. Wrap-up still exists, because the interaction is ACD.

lessons.title: Preferred scores are 0 to 100, and the list has a size
outcomes: Architect’s agent-score collection supports 20 pairs unless Customer Care raises it. More than 20 fails a call flow.

lessons.title: STA reads the conversation after the channel has it
outcomes: Speech and text analytics covers voice and digital interactions. It is not a second ACD.

lessons.title: Sentiment is a label on the text, not a mood you can argue with
outcomes: Sentiment scores the customer’s language. Use it as a filter, then listen.

lessons.title: Topics, programs, and phrases are the dictionary
outcomes: A program groups topics. A topic is phrases you expect to hear or read.

lessons.title: Agent empathy is a detected behavior, still a form question
outcomes: Empathy detection points at calls. Calibration still decides what empathy means for your company.

lessons.title: Content search is how you test the dictionary
outcomes: Search the transcript before you trust a topic count.

lessons.title: Full analysis and a faster transcript are different clocks
outcomes: Some views wait until the interaction is complete. A lower-latency transcript path is a different API.

lessons.title: WEM is a set of products, and WFM is one of them
outcomes: Recording, screen recording, quality, performance, speech and text analytics, and workforce management are the WEM list.

lessons.title: Business units and management units
outcomes: A business unit is the planning container. A management unit is the group of agents you actually schedule.

lessons.title: Service goal templates are the planning target
outcomes: The queue’s service level and the WFM template should describe the same promise.

lessons.title: Schedules are the plan agents work
outcomes: A schedule is built from the management unit, the goals, and activity codes. It is not a routing method.

lessons.title: Intraday and adherence compare the plan to the floor
outcomes: Adherence is the gap between the activity you scheduled and the status the agent is actually in.

lessons.title: Time off is a schedule change with a rule
outcomes: Time-off requests are part of WFM. An approved request that nobody reflects on the schedule is a rumor.

lessons.title: The workforce certification is a named exam
outcomes: The catalog lists a Workforce Management specialist certification and a preparation course. It does not list a code this lab is willing to invent.

lessons.title: A forecast has a short view and a long view
outcomes: Short-term data can build a schedule. The long-term view is for seasonality and does not generate one.

lessons.title: Generate one schedule from a forecast that covers it
outcomes: The schedule period has to sit inside the short-term forecast, and a business unit generates one schedule at a time.
